text:
incident-bot: Pager: spike in 5xxs for /v1/generate — canary rollout for model 'redwood-3b-quant' in eu-west-1 showing 18% error rate, ~30% of requests being rerouted to fallback variant. Auto-fallback is sticky. Notifying on-call. @alice_oncall :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: seeing it, pulling logs now. any customer complaints?

elaine_cs: CS queue has 2 customers reporting high latency; one says responses truncated in EU region.

frank_metrics: metric spike graph: eu-west-1 error rate up from 0.3% -> 18% at 12:02 UTC, p50 latency +90ms, p95 +400ms. Canary traffic is 15%.

ben_platform: likely interaction between canary model and smart-routing fallback. early hypothesis: failing canary causes requests to fall back to older variant in us-east; sticky affinity pins sessions to fallback, causing cross-region route churn.

carla_sre: can we confirm which policy kicked in? routing logs?

alice_oncall: tailing router logs, see repeated route decisions: request set -> canary eu-west -> fail -> fallback variant us-east -> subsequent requests from same session still routed to us-east due to sticky affinity TTL 24h. That explains the sustained spikiness.

ben_platform: that TTL should not persist across model switchover. looks like a policy mismatch: canary flagged as unhealthy but fallback kept sticky binding.

dave_prod: what's customer impact level? are paid customers affected?

elaine_cs: two paying customers in EU on dedicated capacity experiencing degraded responses; their traffic volume is small but they care about SLA.

carla_sre: mitigation plan: (1) pause canary rollout, (2) clear session affinity for impacted routes to allow rebalancing, (3) disable sticky fallback for canaries, (4) roll back canary if needed. Thoughts?

alice_oncall: agreed. implementing step 1 now.

deploy-bot: Received request: pause-rollout redwood-3b-quant canary id=canary-2029. Issuing pause...

deploy-bot: Pause accepted, canary traffic immediately set to 0%.

ben_platform: good. step 2: how to clear sticky affinity without a mass invalidation that impacts other sessions? we can target the routing-table entries for canary tag or flush TTL for sessions routed in last 30m.

carla_sre: running this command to clear affinity for keys with tag "canary-2029":
```
redwoodctl routing flush-affinity --selector "tag:canary-2029" --age 30m
```

carla_sre: running now. expecting propagation within ~15s.

frank_metrics: seeing immediate drop in cross-region handoffs. p50 latency returning to baseline, error rate in eu-west trending down from 18% -> 2% within 90s.

elaine_cs: pinged customers letting them know we paused rollout and are investigating. one asked for timeline for full rollback.

dave_prod: do we need to do a formal rollback or canary fix? block rollout for now and open a ticket for root cause.

ben_platform: need root cause before reattempt. early signs point to tokenization mismatch with quantized weights causing OOM-esque failures in long context. logs show repeated "kv_cache allocation failed" in eu-west.

alice_oncall: capturing failure traces and core dumps, starting a deeper debug run against canary artifact.

carla_sre: setting incident status: mitigated (canary paused, affinity flush done), impact: partial for a few EU customers, severity: sev2 for now.

elaine_cs: customers acknowledged the update, will loop back with product for SLA credit assessment.

ben_platform: follow-ups: (A) disable sticky fallback for canaries until we implement affinity invalidation on canary state changes, (B) reproduce kv allocation on staging with same seq lengths, (C) add automated canary health check that simulates long-context requests. I'll create action items.

alice_oncall: leaving the thread to hand off to morning on-call in 45m. handoff note: canary paused, affinity flush completed, artifacts & traces saved at s3://incidents/2891123456/. Contact ben_platform for root cause updates.

incident-bot: Incident recorded: #2891123456 — Canary-smart-routing affinity loop. State: mitigated. Pager cleared.
